title: EPA’s 2020 Oil and Gas Rule Rescinded Methane Standards; Congress Disapproved It in 2021
description_short: EPA’s August 2020 rule rescinded methane standards for production and processing and methane/VOC standards for transmission and storage; Congress disapproved it in 2021.
description_medium: On August 13, 2020, EPA issued final policy amendments to oil and natural gas New Source Performance Standards. The amendments removed the transmission and storage segment and rescinded methane and VOC standards for that segment, plus methane standards for production and processing. Congress later disapproved the 2020 policy amendments; EPA says they were no longer in effect as of June 30, 2021.
description_long: On August 13, 2020, EPA issued final policy amendments to the 2012 and 2016 New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) for the oil and natural gas industry. The policy amendments removed the transmission and storage segment from the standards and rescinded VOC and methane emissions standards for that segment. They also rescinded methane emissions standards for the production and processing segments. EPA said the policy amendments would make it simpler and less burdensome for the industry to comply. A joint congressional resolution disapproving the 2020 amendments was signed into law in June 2021. EPA states that those amendments were no longer in effect as of June 30, 2021. The 2020 policy amendments were a separate action from technical amendments EPA issued the same day. The record is limited to the methane-related policy changes and their later congressional disapproval; it does not combine the separate technical rule changes with this event.
